name: ottolenghi cherry tomatoes
instructions:
Ottolenghi's hot charred cherry tomatoes over fridge-cold yogurt — the whole dish is the temperature contrast: tomatoes straight out of the oven, yogurt straight out of the fridge, the heat melting the yogurt invitingly. Crusty sourdough or focaccia to mop it up is a must alongside.

SERVES 4 as a starter or part of a mezze plate.

=== INGREDIENTS ===

- 12 1/4 oz (350g) cherry tomatoes
- 3 tbsp olive oil
- 3/4 tsp cumin seeds
- 1/2 tsp light brown sugar (CAREFUL — see the failure mode note)
- 3 garlic cloves, thinly sliced
- 3 thyme sprigs
- 6 oregano sprigs: 3 left whole, the rest stemmed, to serve (fresh oregano is important — see notes)
- 1 lemon: finely shave the skin of 1/2 into 3 strips (I SKIP THESE — see notes), finely grate the other 1/2 for 1 tsp zest
- flaked sea salt and black pepper
- 1 2/3 cups (350g) extra-thick greek-style yogurt, FRIDGE-COLD
- 1 tsp urfa chile flakes (or 1/2 tsp other crushed red pepper flakes)

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. PREHEAT the oven to 425°F.
2. ROAST: toss the tomatoes in a bowl with the olive oil, cumin seeds, sugar, garlic, thyme, oregano sprigs, lemon strips (if using), 1/2 tsp flaked salt, and a good grind of pepper. Transfer to a baking sheet JUST LARGE ENOUGH to fit the tomatoes snugly (~6x8 in). Ottolenghi: roast ~2 in beneath the broiler for 20 minutes until blistering and bubbling, then switch to BROIL for 6-8 minutes until the tomatoes start to blacken on top. MY VERSION: skip the broiler step — just keep it at 425°F for 40 MINUTES while you make other things. That was fine.
3. THE YOGURT: while the tomatoes roast, combine the cold yogurt with the grated lemon zest and 1/4 tsp flaked salt. Keep in the fridge until serving.
4. ASSEMBLE: spread the chilled yogurt on a lipped platter or wide shallow bowl, creating a dip with the back of a spoon. Spoon the HOT tomatoes and all their juices on top, along with the garlic and herbs. Finish with the reserved oregano leaves and the chile flakes. SERVE AT ONCE.
notes:
=== SOURCE ===

Ottolenghi (hot charred cherry tomatoes with cold yogurt). Very good — pass.

=== FAILURE MODE — TOO MUCH BROWN SUGAR ===

Easy to overdo the brown sugar: it's HARD TO TASTE BEFORE IT GOES IN THE OVEN, and whatever you add gets AMPLIFIED after baking (the roast concentrates it). Stick to the 1/2 tsp; err under.

=== MY DEVIATIONS (BOTH FINE) ===

- SKIPPED THE BROILER STEP: just 425°F for 40 minutes straight while making other things. Fine.
- SKIPPED THE LEMON STRIPS: just the zest in the yogurt. The strips-in-the-roast step isn't needed.

=== FRESH OREGANO IS IMPORTANT ===

Fresh oregano matters here — and this dish is a GOOD EXCUSE TO BUY IT. (Half the sprigs roast in whole; the stemmed leaves finish the dish fresh.)

=== THE TEMPERATURE CONTRAST IS THE DISH ===

Ottolenghi's framing: tomatoes straight out of the oven, yogurt straight out of the fridge — the hot tomatoes melt the cold yogurt on contact. Don't let either equilibrate. Bread (crusty sourdough or focaccia) is a must to mop it up.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[sweet-potato-pies-and-galettes]]: the other yogurt/aleppo-adjacent register (urfa is aleppo's darker cousin — the raisiny one).
- [[kachumber]] / [[indian-mashed-eggplant]]: the other yogurt-and-vegetable mezze neighbors.
- [[tartine]]: bread-that-mops territory.
